content.comment_body: Hello! I am working on designing an [product_name] interface between a Nest thermostat and a fan coil unit. The unit uses two 3-way valves, for heating and cooling, operated by 24VAC electric actuators that need a 0-10V signal for valve positioning. From the manual, it seems [product_name] expansion modules only offer analog DC outputs. Is there a recommended solution to generate a 0-10VAC output? Thank you! Best regards, [user_name] in London
Do you have a description or a [url] for the valves? I haven't come across a 0-10VAC signal before.
Here’s the data sheet—these valves are commonly found in commercial HVAC systems from Sauter.
I don’t see any reference to a 0...10VAC signal. As far as I can tell, it’s just a 0...10V signal, which is DC, not AC.
I assumed the control signal would be AC due to the 24VAC supply, but you’re right! This simplifies things, thank you for your help.
Good luck with your project. Having a second perspective can be really helpful sometimes ...

analysis.insight_summary: Users debated how to link [product_name] hardware to valve actuators believed to need a 0-10VAC analog signal. Through discussion, they clarified the actuators actually use a 0-10V DC signal, which fits the output from [product_name] expansion modules. The main UX insight is that confusion can easily arise when documentation and signal/power labeling conventions overlap or are unclear.
analysis.user_expectations: The user initially expected [product_name] modules to deliver analog AC output, believing actuator control signals matched their 24VAC power supply. Overall, the expectation was for direct compatibility between [product_name] expansion module outputs and valve actuator input requirements.
